source_claim: Clear Envelope in the Clip View envelope context menu resets the selected clip envelope to its default. Exact default values and the source’s shortcut-to-menu wording remain unresolved; parameter Delete Automation is a distinct context.
documentary_expected: Clear Envelope in the Clip View envelope context menu resets the selected clip envelope to its default. Exact default values and the source’s shortcut-to-menu wording remain unresolved; parameter Delete Automation is a distinct context.
documentary_comparator: Compare only named visible control/state predicates; compound signal/timing clauses remain ungraded, with no numerical or runtime parity proof.

title: MIDI Envelope Auto-Reset option
setup_and_action: F-MIDI: known nonempty MIDI clip and separately positive controller destination; inspect option availability/state in each documented context. Message capture is an ungraded future probe; no all-controller reset is assumed.
source_claim: MIDI Envelope Auto-Reset is offered through Options or the Sample Editor context menu and is described as resetting certain MIDI control messages at new clip start. Which messages/values, delivery time and persistence are unknown.

title: Non-destructive sample modulation
setup_and_action: F-AUDIO: retain identical owned source hash shared by two clips with distinct active envelopes and positive output, edit one envelope and observe source identity/audio separately. Export/consolidation is not executed and no codec or waveform oracle is supplied.
source_claim: Clip-envelope modulation is non-destructive to the referenced sample on disk; clips can reuse one sample with different envelopes. Render/resample/consolidate are separate ways to commit audio, owned by their workflow pages.

title: Audio transposition envelope context
setup_and_action: F-AUDIO: positively playing warped owned pitched sample, nonzero admitted Transpose base and envelope; inspect Clip/Transposition and fine edits, compare accepted Warp contexts in reset trials. Retain no DSP/timing expectation.
source_claim: The audio Clip/Transposition workflow uses Warp on and supports Draw Mode or fine breakpoint edits. The source describes additive influence bounded by the Transpose range and Warp-mode/granularity-dependent response; no frequency law, warp kernel, smoothing or numeric event conversion is added.

title: Audio Clip Gain modulation role
setup_and_action: F-AUDIO: independently positive source and nonzero Clip Gain, active nonzero envelope; compare upper setting and attenuation in reset copies using paired dry/active baselines. No waveform gain ratio or silence floor oracle.
source_claim: Clip/Gain envelope can shape sample level. Its influence is relative to Clip Gain, can attenuate to silence and cannot exceed that absolute setting; this documentary role supplies no calibrated gain-domain formula.

title: Sample Offset eligibility
setup_and_action: F-AUDIO: nonempty independently positive rhythmic sample, Warp on; compare Beats and another actually offered mode with nonzero offset envelope retained for the Beats positive trial. Grade visible eligibility only.
source_claim: Clip/Sample Offset modulation is available only in Beats Warp Mode and is edited as a clip envelope. The chapter’s beat-scrambling examples do not establish random, resampling or analytic cut-and-splice behavior.

title: Track volume stage and indicator
setup_and_action: F-AUDIO: enabled audible effect, nonzero Track Volume and distinct Clip Gain modulation; inspect target identities and slider dot while manually changing the base. Numerical output remains U.
source_claim: Clip Gain and Track Volume are distinct envelope targets; Track Volume modulation affects the mixer’s post-effect gain stage and a dot below its slider indicates the modulated setting. No stored-unit or signal multiplier law is restated.
documentary_expected: Clip Gain and Track Volume are distinct envelope targets; Track Volume modulation affects the mixer’s post-effect gain stage and a dot below its slider indicates the modulated setting. No stored-unit or signal multiplier law is restated.

title: Send modulation ceiling role
setup_and_action: F-AUDIO: nonzero send to independently positive nonmuted wet return with correct monitoring, active nonzero envelope and a paired positive return baseline. Compare attenuation/upper role without a numerical or silence-threshold oracle.
source_claim: Send modulation is relative to the Send control: it cannot open the send beyond the knob and can reduce it to minus infinity. This does not extend finite send coefficients or define event conversion.

title: Pan modulation contextual range
setup_and_action: F-AUDIO: independently positive distinguishable stereo path, admitted nonzero pan envelope; establish centered positive modulation, then an intermediate base and full-left control on reset copies. Confirm active envelope and output before no-effect observation; no channel equality metric.
source_claim: Pan modulation range depends on the base knob: center permits the full stereo span, movement toward an edge reduces available influence, and full left is described as no-effect. This is not a pan law or formula for every mode.

title: Device modulation relative role
setup_and_action: F-AUDIO: an actually eligible device target with active section, nonzero base/amount and independently positive processed output; compare two admitted base settings while keeping envelope. No unsupported target or preset replacement is inferred.
source_claim: Clip modulation acts on devices in that clip’s track and changes controls relative to their current setting rather than defining preset values. Per-device eligible targets and combination arithmetic require their owners/evidence.

title: MIDI controller envelope editing
setup_and_action: F-MIDI: independently valid MIDI clip and known listed controller, edit a nonzero changing envelope, inspect imported/recorded indicator in separately accepted fixtures. Receiver path/data semantics remain U.
source_claim: MIDI Ctrl/Control selects listed controller envelopes for creation/editing with steps or points, including imported/recorded data indicated by adjacent LEDs. Most controller numbers through 119 are described as supported; this is not every number or a MIDI codec. Receiver conventions may differ from names such as Pitch Bend or Pan.

title: Envelope-local region controls
setup_and_action: F-LOOP: positive warped looping sample and a known active envelope; unlink that envelope and toggle its Loop off/on, inspect sample Loop unchanged. Playback duration/phase/reset remains a separate ungraded observation.
source_claim: Unlinking gives the selected envelope its own local region/loop controls and colored loop braces. Its Loop switch is independent of the sample’s Loop switch, allowing a one-shot envelope while the sample continues looping.
documentary_expected: Unlinking gives the selected envelope its own local region/loop controls and colored loop braces. Its Loop switch is independent of the sample’s Loop switch, allowing a one-shot envelope while the sample continues looping.

title: Independent envelope lengths and start markers
setup_and_action: F-LOOP: positive sample loop and two admitted unlinked envelopes with distinct nonzero lengths and starts; inspect controls at two zoom levels and an offered non-bar length. Retain phase/clock observations ungraded.
source_claim: Each unlinked envelope can have its own loop length, extended by braces or numeric controls, including non-bar-aligned lengths. Its start marker identifies where envelope playback begins on clip start; start/end and braces obey the zoom-adaptive grid. No clip-time equation or sample-rounded extent follows.

title: Local-loop rhythmic role
setup_and_action: F-LOOP: independently positive long source and short envelope, then short source and long envelope on reset copies. Hide grid and adjust admitted local endpoints. Observe repeated control/audio influence with no period, beat/sample or synchronization comparator.
source_claim: Local envelope loops may be shorter or longer than source playback and can be shaped with handles/shapes. The source describes tempo-relative repetition and grid-hidden independent endpoints; it does not specify clock arithmetic, rate limits or a free-running oscillator implementation.

title: Linked envelope Warp interaction
setup_and_action: F-LOOP: positive warped clip, Linked envelope and two independently identified markers; move an interior marker via ordinary editor then envelope editor in reset copies. Inspect visible relative envelope change; no exact time conversion or waveform oracle.
source_claim: In Linked mode, moving a clip Warp Marker lengthens/shortens its envelope accordingly, and Warp Markers can be adjusted within the envelope editor. Exact marker/envelope transformation and interpolation stay unknown or with the finite Warp owner.

title: Record events
setup_and_action: F-REC: record an independently changing accepted parameter over beats 1-4 and a second loop with Automation Arm/appropriate record and actual running transport confirmed. Retain resulting envelope/event inventory only through understood format; no point thinning, Id, sentinel, overwrite-bound or codec oracle.

title: Value return
setup_and_action: F-OVERRIDE: two independently active envelopes, recording off, positive output; compare per-target re-enable, global re-enable and automated clip relaunch on reset copies. Capture indicator/value/audio return around events, without assuming immediate jumps, ramps, clip-time reset or Back to Arrangement equivalence.

title: Arrangement return
setup_and_action: F-VIEWS: establish positive Arrangement envelope and a different Session envelope; launch, stop Session and request Back to Arrangement in separate trials using existing owners. Keep nonzero source/output and explicit transport; record ownership without extending mix-graph A8 beyond its finite scope.

title: Clear shortcut
setup_and_action: F-EDITOR: on reset copies focus parameter, Session Envelope Editor and Arrangement lane separately with a retained positive altered envelope, then use documented platform deletion shortcut or menu. Record whether menu/direct clear/delete is offered; local source wording supplies no dispatch oracle.

title: Replacement
setup_and_action: F-AUDIO: two owned positive samples with known equal duration, then a different duration in separate trials. Retain envelope and Warp-marker before-inventory, replace sample via existing CV041 owner, compare identities/settings. Do not adopt the clip chapter all-settings wording as marker preservation for unequal samples.

title: Midi auto reset
setup_and_action: F-MIDI: with independently accepted controller destination and positive nonzero envelope messages, compare Auto-Reset off/on while launching a different clip. Capture actual messages only with available path; unknown message set, values and timing stay null.

title: Mapped overwrite
setup_and_action: F-MAPPING/F-REC: establish accepted unique MIDI assignment and takeover preference using mapping owner, positive nonzero parameter excursion and active recording first. Compare mouse, MIDI knob and key input separately with recording on/off. No takeover, latch interval or universal key-recording rule is borrowed.

title: Tempo range
setup_and_action: F-MAPPING: independently active nonzero tempo automation, known accepted assigned controller and actual min/max controls; compare two admitted display ranges while transport runs then stops. Retain control/value traces without controller normalization, numeric range repair or global-clock oracle.

title: Inactive controls
setup_and_action: F-REC/F-AUDIO: first establish recorded automation and active eligible target with nonzero output/base/depth. Then separately disable Automation Arm/record or relevant section/route and edit one parameter. Compare paired positive trial; inactive/silent paths cannot prove no-effect or a universal refusal.

title: Empty and edges
setup_and_action: F-EDITOR: compare a proper nonempty time selection and three separated valid points against empty lane, marker only, exact envelope/clip/loop edge and equal-time candidates in reset copies. Use offered edits only; no reader normalization, event sorting, refusal or half-open endpoint law.

title: Transform limits
setup_and_action: F-EDITOR: independently valid interior transform first, then drag handles across each other, collapse width/height or cross outside neighbors in separate copies. Record admitted state, clipping and point loss without formulas or a guaranteed repair.

title: Target contexts
setup_and_action: F-REC: start from positive ordinary-track automation, then inspect actually offered targets on group, return, Main and multi-clip selections separately. Preserve valid positive source/receiver paths; broad all-target support is not inferred from practically-all wording.

title: Undo redo
setup_and_action: F-EDITOR/F-REC: on separate copies perform insertion, drag/drop overwrite, clear, transform, recording pass and override/re-enable. Undo then Redo with complete point/control/route before-inventory. No grouping, file or override restoration oracle.

title: Cancel
setup_and_action: F-EDITOR: begin point/segment/handle drag or typed value edit, then use actually offered Escape/cancel before commit; separately dismiss shape/clear menu. Retain preview versus committed state, no atomic rollback law.

title: Save reopen
setup_and_action: F-REC/F-OVERRIDE: save/reopen owned Set after record, unlinked edits, override and re-enable separately, with source/controller/target present then absent in copies. Inventory envelopes, link/loop state and visible arm/filter/override state; storage/evaluator owners do not imply UI persistence.

title: Transport loop
setup_and_action: F-LOOP/F-REC: positive active automation with explicit record/arm and source/output; stop/start, seek, loop, change 120 to 90 BPM and meter on separate copies. Capture point/control traces without expected release, reset, beat conversion or event race order.

title: Rate engine
setup_and_action: F-REC: repeat positive pass at actually supported 44.1/48/96 kHz and 64/512-frame blocks, then request rate/block change or engine restart while recording on separate copies. Retain pre-change baseline; no sample-aligned equality, event count or smoothing invariant.

title: Target removal
setup_and_action: F-AUDIO/F-REC: independently active nonzero source/envelope/output first; remove target device, clip or track separately while recording/playing or while a transform is pending. Inventory references, other paths and diagnostics without guessed rebinding, silence or cleanup.

title: Source controller loss
setup_and_action: F-MAPPING/F-AUDIO: retain positive source and accepted controller delivery, then make only owned media or available controller port absent in separate copies during automation. Record output/record state and recovery; no absent capability is simulated.

title: Malformed
setup_and_action: F-EDITOR: on owned copies enter abc, NaN or out-of-domain numeric text only in an offered editable control; a malformed saved envelope is used only through independently understood storage-owner format. No hidden parser/schema or all-errors refusal is invented.

title: Close active
setup_and_action: F-REC/F-LOOP: while positive automation recording, unlinked playback or a pending transform is active, close/replace Set or quit through offered controls in separate copies. Record prompts, retained state and output without completion, flush, silence or resource deadline.

title: Concurrent edit
setup_and_action: F-REC: independently changing accepted parameter and positive output with running transport; attempt an offered envelope edit, target move/removal or clear during record, separately stop and retry. Record eligibility and resulting inventory, no snapshot-time or transaction ordering law.
